headline: Wounded at Anfield, Villarreal are narrow favourites at Mestalla
summary: Valencia are 19th in La Liga with 6 points, so Saturday's derby at Mestalla is a pressure game for them. Villarreal arrive from a 4-3 defeat at Anfield on Wednesday and have had only 4 days to recover; Valencia have had 7. Two La Liga draws, with Racing Santander and Athletic Club, have stopped Valencia's slide, and Copete may return after the knee injury he suffered against Villarreal. Even so, the market makes Villarreal 44% favourites, and the handicap gives Valencia a quarter of a goal. The total-goals line is 2.75, with the over at 49.6%.
read: Valencia are 19th with one win in nine and need this derby to relieve the pressure on Javier Aguirre, but they host a Villarreal side that has won three of the last five meetings and creates far more (2.02 xG per game to Valencia's 1.10). Villarreal are the 44.0% favourites but arrive four days after throwing away a 2-0 lead at Anfield, so the market still makes it only a quarter-goal game, with around three goals expected.

facts.fact: Valencia sit 19th in La Liga with 6 points from 9 games — one win, three draws, five defeats and a goal difference of -9.
facts.meaning: The home side are in the relegation places and this regional derby is a pressure game for them, not a free hit.

facts.fact: Villarreal are the market's favourites at 44.0% to win at Mestalla, against Valencia's 30.1%.
facts.meaning: The visitors are clearly the more likely winners, but not by a landslide — over a quarter of the market's weight sits on the draw.

facts.fact: Villarreal lost 4-3 at Liverpool in the Champions League on Tuesday after leading 2-0, as reported by The Guardian.
facts.meaning: They arrive at Mestalla off a painful collapse rather than a smooth run-in, and with the emotional cost of a European away night.

facts.fact: Villarreal have 4 days between that Anfield match and kick-off; Valencia have had 7 since their 0-0 with Athletic Club.
The market's 50/50 handicap line has Valencia receiving a quarter goal — the fair line is +0.27 from the home perspective.
facts.meaning: Villarreal are rated only about a quarter of a goal better than a side sitting 19th, so the market expects a tight, one-goal-ish game.

facts.fact: Villarreal created 2.38 xG at home to Elche last weekend and drew 0-0.
facts.meaning: Chance creation is not their problem; turning it into goals has been — a warning for a Valencia defence that will sit deeper.

facts.fact: The market's 50/50 goal line sits at 2.75, with Over priced at 49.6%.
facts.meaning: The market sees roughly three goals — a game with chances at both ends rather than a cagey 0-0.

facts.fact: Villarreal are unbeaten in the last five meetings with Valencia — three wins and two draws — including 2-1 in February and 0-2 at Mestalla last October.
facts.meaning: This fixture has been one-way traffic for a while, and Villarreal have won at Mestalla in this calendar year.

sources.fact: OneFootball reports that Javier Aguirre's Valencia need a win in this high-stakes regional derby at Mestalla to ease the pressure after a difficult start.
Valencia manager Javier Aguirre expressed delight with Harvey Elliott's work ethic and sharper physical shape during his loan spell.
OneFootball reports that Javier Aguirre has steadied Valencia, with two scored and two conceded across meetings with Racing de Santander and Athletic Club, and that the injury list is easing.
Super Eagles striker Umar Sadiq, sidelined since an injury in September, is nearing a return for Valencia.
Copete could return for Valencia against Villarreal, seven months after suffering a serious knee injury against the same opponent.
El Desmarque reports that Copete, seven months after his serious knee injury against Villarreal, is seeing light at the end of the tunnel and could feature in this match.
Superdeporte reports that Aguirre's main concern ahead of the Villarreal match is the defensive help from his wingers.
Villarreal lost 4-3 to Liverpool at Anfield in the Champions League after leading 2-0.
